stories.title: Neo4j Launches Context Engine: A Shared Knowledge Layer for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.body: On October 20, 2026, Neo4j announced the Neo4j Context Engine — a reusable, shared substrate that allows AI agents to consistently reason over enterprise knowledge. The product includes a six-layer Business Ontology that maps an organization's processes, data, and AI assets into a graph, plus a graph-native memory layer that gives agents memory and reinforced learning from past decisions. It also logs agent reasoning and operational paths to form a permanent record of enterprise experience.
stories.why: This is a direct proof point for the data foundation argument: without a governed knowledge layer, agents hallucinate or contradict each other across systems. A Graas seller can use this launch to show prospects that the market has converged on context-layer-first architecture — and that any agent deployment without it (including competitors') is building on sand.

stories.title: McKinsey: 'Who Wins When AI Does the Shopping?' — Global Survey of 21,000 Consumers Finds Retailer AI Assistants Trail Stand-Alone Tools by 2x
stories.body: McKinsey's Agentic Commerce Consumer Survey (fielded June 2026, ~21,000 respondents across 11 markets) found that the rate at which US AI users completed a purchase with AI jumped 70% over the prior year. However, retailer-owned AI assistants trail stand-alone AI tools by as much as two times throughout the shopping journey, only catching up at checkout. Overall, 56% of consumers used an AI chat or search tool in the past three months versus 27% who used a retailer's own AI shopping assistant.
stories.why: The 2x gap between third-party AI tools and in-house retailer assistants is a compelling data point that directly explains why enterprise retailers need better-grounded agents — the ones losing ground are the ones without a solid context and data layer. Graas sellers can cite this October 2026 McKinsey study to explain why the architecture problem must be solved before an agent goes live.

stories.title: McKinsey & EuroCommerce Report: European Retail AI Has Stalled at the Pilot Stage — Scaling Is Now the Defining Challenge
stories.body: The June 2026 report 'Rewiring Retail in Europe: The AI Imperative' (McKinsey + EuroCommerce, survey of 36 retail executives) estimates that end-to-end AI transformation could unlock €240–320 billion in economic value for European retail over five years, equivalent to a four-to-ten percentage-point improvement in operating profit. Despite this, only around 30% of organizations report advanced capabilities in AI governance, risk, and control, while a further third lack formal frameworks entirely. The report identifies 'becoming agent-ready' — meaning connected data, commercial decision-making, and supply chain — as a top priority for retailers to escape the pilot trap.
stories.why: The governance and data-readiness gap is the exact reason AI pilots stall, and McKinsey names it explicitly. Graas sellers can point to this report when a prospect says their agents 'aren't working yet' — the root cause is almost always the missing context and governance layer, not the agent model itself.

stories.title: Salesforce Completes $3.6B Acquisition of Fin (Formerly Intercom Fin), Folding It Into Agentforce
stories.body: Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin — the customer-service AI company formerly known as Intercom — on September 10, 2026, for approximately $3.6 billion, with Fin now operating inside Salesforce AI Labs. The deal brings more than 30,000 business customers to Salesforce and adds Fin's autonomous support technology — which Salesforce says resolves 76% of support volume without a human — into the Agentforce platform. Fin is priced at $0.99 per resolved outcome and is designed for rapid deployment on existing help desks, in contrast to Agentforce's deeply customizable enterprise offering.
stories.why: This consolidation fundamentally reshapes the competitive landscape: Intercom Fin is now a Salesforce product, bundled with CRM, which raises the switching cost for any retailer on Salesforce. Graas sellers competing in accounts that use Salesforce must now explain the difference between a bundled, lightly configured agent and a purpose-built, context-grounded retail agent — and what that difference means for resolution quality and outcome reliability.

stories.title: Sierra AI Raises $950M at $15.8B Valuation, Launches 'Horizon' for Long-Horizon Agent Goals; Decagon Hits $4.5B on $250M Round
stories.body: Sierra raised $950 million led by Tiger Global and GV in May 2026 at a $15.8 billion valuation, reporting over $150M in ARR and claiming it serves over 40% of the Fortune 50. In July 2026, Sierra launched Horizon — acquired via Takeoff — extending agents to goals that unfold over days or weeks (examples: loan origination, healthcare prior authorization). Rival Decagon raised $250 million in January 2026 at a $4.5 billion valuation, adding 100+ corporate clients including Avis Budget Group and Deutsche Telekom, and in March 2026 launched persistent memory of past conversations plus outbound voice.
stories.why: Sierra and Decagon are the two agents most likely to appear on a prospect's shortlist alongside or instead of Graas. Sierra's move into long-horizon, multi-day agent goals signals where the enterprise CX category is heading; Decagon's rapid client acquisition shows the mid-market is moving fast. Graas sellers need to be able to articulate what a retail-specific, catalog-and-inventory-grounded agent delivers that neither of these horizontal platforms can match out of the box.
